After every `os.open`, the caller MUST: (i) read `current_mode = stat.S_IMODE(os.fstat(fd).st_mode)`; (ii) if `current_mode != mode` AND the file is owned by caller-uid, call `os.fchmod(fd, mode)` to coerce existing file to the mode invariant; (iii) if `os.fchmod` raises (`PermissionError` due to read-only mount, alien owner, ACL conflict on Windows NTFS, etc.), FAIL CLOSED — propagate the exception rather than proceeding with non-conforming perms (the audit-trail invariant is enforced everywhere or fails loudly). Document in commit body for any consumer applying this rule: one-time migration shell command `find .claude/state -name '*.jsonl' -perm /044 -exec chmod 0600 {} +` (POSIX) OR `Get-ChildItem -Path .claude/state -Filter *.jsonl -Recurse | Where-Object { ($_ | Get-Acl).AccessToString -match 'Everyone Allow Read' } | ForEach-Object { icacls $_.FullName /inheritance:r /grant ${env:USERNAME}:F }` (Windows) for legacy `mcp_health.jsonl` / `subagent_transcripts.jsonl` / `codex_postcommit_reviews.jsonl` / `subagent_start.jsonl` / `worktree_lifecycle_audit.jsonl` files created at `0o644` per pre-Round-6 mandates. Take an **exclusive advisory lock** (`fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX)` on POSIX / `msvcrt.locking` on Windows); **if neither primitive is available, or if the platform does not enforce advisory locks (e.g., NFS without NLM support), FAIL CLOSED — raise rather than proceeding without a lock** (per Round-5 F-2 NFS-silent-succeed finding). **Windows separate-lockfile mechanism** *(Round-7c per T3 round-7b NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 NEW-CLASS finding on commit `48c49fb` caught by codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE)*: `msvcrt.locking` locks `nbytes` from CURRENT file-pointer position, NOT the whole file like POSIX `fcntl.flock`. Under O_APPEND the JSONL fd's pointer moves on each write, breaking lock-release symmetry (LK_UNLCK at the new pointer would find no lock at the byte LK_LOCK was issued for). Round-7b workaround (shipped at `scripts/_atomic_jsonl_append.py:_acquire_lock(fd, path)` commit `48c49fb`): open separate `<jsonl-path>.lock` file with 1-byte placeholder + lock byte 0 of the LOCKFILE (no writes to lockfile means file pointer stays at byte 0). Module returns `lock_fd` for Windows callers to release; `None` for POSIX. **Lock-protocol rollout constraint** *(Round-7c per same T3 finding)*: when the lock protocol bumps (direct-jsonl-fd → separate-lockfile-v1, or separate-lockfile-v1 → separate-lockfile-v2-versioned), enforce single-version deployment for the entire concurrent-writer cohort. Old + new code locking DIFFERENT lock domains do NOT mutually exclude — concurrent writers can race even though each ALONE acquires its lock correctly. Mitigations (pick ONE before any concurrent rollout): **(i) transitional dual-lock**: acquire both old AND new protocol locks in series during the transition window; **(ii) runtime version-marker**: write protocol-version byte to lockfile + fail-closed on read-version-mismatch (FORWARD-REF for v2 lock protocol bump); **(iii) single-version cohort barrier**: coordinate cohort upgrade via deployment system before any new-version runs. Currently sss has ZERO consumers of `_atomic_jsonl_append.py` (FORWARD-REF wire-up Ships 2-5 pending per `tmp/wave22-orchestrator-salvage-jsonl-mode-bits-audit-2026-05-05.md`), so the version-skew window is THEORETICAL until first hook migrates to use the module. Future protocol bumps MUST honor one of (i)/(ii)/(iii). HOLD the lock across BOTH (a) JSON-encoding the record AND (b) the single low-level `os.write(fd, encoded_bytes)` — never use buffered text writes (`f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")` via Python file objects can split into multiple writes). **If JSON encoding raises (`UnicodeEncodeError`, non-serializable type), release the lock and propagate the exception — do not silently drop the record** (per Round-5 F-3 silent-record-drop finding). For records where **`len(encoded_bytes)` — the byte count AFTER JSON encoding, NOT the key count of the dict —** exceeds the platform atomic-write bound (≤PIPE_BUF 4KB POSIX; ≤512 bytes for Windows or treat the lock as the sole correctness boundary), reject the record OR shard via option (b) filename-namespace; do NOT silently truncate (per Round-5 F-5 measurement-target finding).
